faq.a: Khulud is associated with the Arabic form خلود, whose core sense is immortality, eternity.

faq.q: What is the origin of Khulud?
faq.a: Khulud is associated with Arabic. Khulud is Arabic خُلُود (Khulūd) 'immortality, eternity', from the root خ ل د (kh-l-d). The source gloss 'Eternal, Everlasting' is broadly consistent. Same name as khalood, khaloud, kholud, khulood and khuloud.
Yes — the underlying form خلود is Arabic.
Khulud can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Khulud should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. False

faq.q: What does Khulud mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Khulud is rendered خلود and carries the sense خلود، ہمیشگی، بقا.

faq.q: What does Khulud mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Khulud is rendered خلود and carries the sense خلود، جاودانگی، بقا.
A romanized syllable approximation is khu-lud. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Khulud?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Khulud, khulud. Script forms are خلود, ख़ुलूद.

faq.q: Is Khulud a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
